texts: good. the party is one group of twelve people, the departure is a past event with Aelmere as what was left, and sundown, day 33 and Year 1 all sit on that event.
good. Sailsworn is the leader, the party is what is led, the goat-path is the route and the Salt-bloom Tide-pools the destination — every part of the sentence is carried.
good. the coordination is split correctly into two carryings by the party, the copper buckets and the wooden scrapers each as their own set, and both compounds are unpacked to bucket and scraper.
good. Coraline Ash is recorded as walking alongside the party as a companion rather than being asserted a member of it, which is exactly what "with" says.

mixed: the assignment itself parses well and is usable — a fireable rule that gives every party member his or her own pool out of the five, with the "each" recorded — but "the five blooming pools" arrives as a brand-new set with no link back to the Salt-bloom Tide-pools named in sentence 2, so nothing says these are those pools. Put the link in the sentence: "Sailsworn assigned each member of the harvest party to one of the five blooming pools in the Salt-bloom Tide-pools."

bad: the parse makes the second pool from the north one of the five blooming pools — your sentence never says that — and the reasoner then concludes this pool is blooming, content you did not state. If it is one of the five, say so: "Sailsworn assigned Coraline Ash to the second pool from the north, one of the five blooming pools." The ordinal itself (second, counting from the north) is handled fine, so keep that wording.
